binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with an arbitrary measurable-space structure.
A measure mu on Omega, together with the assumption/typeclass that mu is a probability measure.
A real-valued function X : Omega -> Real.
Arbitrary real parameters lambda and a.
hypotheses: X is measurable from Omega to the real numbers with their Borel measurable space.
The pushforward measure of mu by X equals the measure induced by the PMF that gives probability 1/2 to 1 and probability 1/2 to -1. Equivalently, X has the symmetric two-point {1, -1} distribution.
conclusions: The integral over Omega of exp(lambda * (a * X(omega))) with respect to mu equals (exp(lambda*a) + exp(-(lambda*a))) / 2.
The same integral over Omega of exp(lambda * (a * X(omega))) with respect to mu equals cosh(lambda*a).
mathematical_definitions: The discrete law in the hypothesis is obtained by taking a Bernoulli(1/2) Boolean variable and mapping true to 1 and false to -1.
Measure.map X mu is the pushforward distribution of X under mu.
The integral is the real-valued Bochner/Lebesgue integral, so on a probability space it is the expectation of exp(lambda*a*X).
For real t, cosh(t) = (exp(t) + exp(-t)) / 2; the proposition nevertheless states the exponential-average equality and the cosh equality as two distinct conjuncts.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable real-valued random variable X on any probability space whose distribution is symmetric on 1 and -1 with probability 1/2 each, and for every pair of real numbers lambda and a, the expectation of exp(lambda*a*X) is exactly the average of exp(lambda*a) and exp(-lambda*a), and it is also exactly cosh(lambda*a).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result applies only under exact equality of the entire pushforward law of X with the symmetric two-point law; equality of a few moments or merely taking values in {1, -1} is not the stated hypothesis.
The statement constrains X distributionally, not pointwise: it does not assert that X(omega) is literally 1 or -1 for every omega, only that its pushforward measure has that law.

No integrability hypothesis is written explicitly. The integrand is interpreted by the general Bochner integral; under the exact finite two-point law it is expected to be integrable for every fixed real lambda and a, so this creates no apparent vacuous case.
No independence assumptions, auxiliary random variables, bounds on lambda or a, or nonzero assumptions on either parameter are present.
The conjunction contains two logically required conclusions even though their right-hand sides are mathematically equal by the standard identity for cosh.
The premises are satisfiable, for example on a two-point probability space with equal masses, so there is no apparent impossible-premise vacuity.
ambiguities: The one-level bodies shown for Measure.map and MeasureTheory.integral are opaque wrapper projections, so their lower-level implementations are not exposed by the dossier; their standard public mathematical meanings as pushforward measure and Bochner integral are used.

The dossier defines Real.cosh through the real part of complex cosh rather than unfolding complex cosh, so the identity cosh(t) = (exp(t) + exp(-t))/2 is recognized as standard mathematics rather than fully derivable from the displayed one-level dependency bodies alone.
